title: CKD definition and the causes of chronic tubulointerstitial disease
guide: CKD = >5% interstitial fibrosis/tubular atrophy/glomerular sclerosis with fewer functional nephrons. The causes table maps vascular (RAS/TMA), glomerular (IgAN/MPGN/FSGS/membranous and diabetes) causes to secondary tubulointerstitial fibrosis, and primary tubulointerstitial fibrosis to CTID. Pathology is scarring with fibrosis and atrophy >5%.

title: Etiology of CTID: from ciliopathies to metabolic and autoimmune causes
guide: Etiology runs from ciliopathies, reflux nephropathy (VUR) and obstructive nephropathy, through drugs (lithium microcysts; calcineurin-inhibitor striped pattern with afferent arteriolar hyalinosis; PPIs) and toxins (lead saturnine gout; cadmium ouch ouch nephropathy) to metabolic causes (hypercalcemia, hyperuricemia/urate nephropathy, hyperoxaluria, hypokalemic vacuolization of PCT > DCT), then autoimmune causes (sarcoidosis, Sjogren's, IgG4) and finally CKDu.

title: CTID features, investigations and the CKDu concept
guide: CTID is asymptomatic with an insidious onset. The clinical-features table links each sign to its cause: polyuria/nocturia (concentration defect), anaemia (peritubular interstitial fibroblast EPO), nephrogenic DI (cortical collecting duct fibrosis), RTA IV (beta cell fibrosis) and RTA I (alpha intercalated cell fibrosis), with rickets in children from phosphate loss. Anaemia is maximal in CTID and minimal in ADPKD. Investigations: proteinuria <2 g/day with beta-2 microglobulin, inactive sediment, deranged RFT, small kidneys. CKDu: unknown pathophysiology, theories of heat stress, agrochemicals, fluoride, cadmium and communicable disease; eastern coast of India, middle-aged men, asymptomatic until ESRF.
